_readme: THE channel registry. Every channel name a spec may reference resolves here, and
the compiler turns names into the numeric indices TgNode.watchMask, TgAction.channel
and TgTrialType.rewardLine actually hold.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Phase 0's specs name channels -- `left_well`, `odor_line_1`,
`fluid_0` -- and documented them as 'resolved against the box pinout'. No such
artifact existed. Worse, the engagement port and the trial light were named NOWHERE:
every spec's engagement WAIT_ENTRY has to watch the odor port and every LIGHTS_ON /
LIGHTS_OFF has to drive the trial light, but neither appears in any spec, because
both are emitted by the template rather than authored. A compiler cannot produce a
table without this file.
WHY NOT DECLARE CHANNELS PER SPEC. It would reopen the frozen task_spec.v1.json and
repeat the same pinout in five files. Specs already reference channels by name; they
only needed somewhere to resolve against. See docs/decisions.md D15.
WHY NOT PARSE BehaviorBox.h. It is the true single source, and parsing it would
never drift -- but it would couple the compiler to reading C++ out of a repo that is
deliberately read-only, for a table that changes roughly never. The pinout is
transcribed here instead, with the source line for each entry, and a Phase 5 bench
check against the real hardware is the thing that actually validates it.
TRANSCRIBED FROM: Arduino/libraries/BehaviorBox/BehaviorBox.h:55-92 in the firmware
repo. If a pin moves there, it must move here -- and unlike START_LINE_MAX, the
mismatch is loud: a wrong index drives the wrong solenoid, which the Phase 5 jig
catches before any animal does.

kinds.engagement: The port whose entry initiates a trial. EXACTLY ONE channel may carry this kind -- the template resolves the engagement WAIT_ENTRY, the commitment HOLD, every sampling HOLD and the sampling-release WAIT_EXIT to it by kind rather than by name, which is what lets one template serve a box with a different port name.
kinds.response: A port that may appear in topology.response_ports.
kinds.emitter: A stimulus actuator. 'Stimulus' is an emitter channel and nothing more, which is why a speaker or LED substitutes for an odor valve with no interpreter change.
kinds.reward: A reward actuator. Pulse width is the delivered magnitude.
kinds.cue: A trial-availability signal driven by entry actions, not a stimulus.
kinds.vacuum: Odor-routing hardware with no behavioural meaning of its own.

_watch_mask_note: TgNode.watchMask is uint8, so at most 8 channels can be watched simultaneously.
Only `engagement` and `response` channels are ever watched -- emitters, rewards,
cues and the vacuum are write-only -- so the mask indexes WATCHABLE channels, not
all channels. `watch_bit` below is that index and is dense over exactly those.
With one engagement channel that leaves 7 response ports, while task_spec.v1.json
permits 8. A spec that names 8 response ports is a capacity ERROR rather than a
silently dropped port; see the TG5xx rule.

odor_port.rationale: The engagement port. Named in no spec because the template resolves it by kind -- an engagement port is a structural fact of the epoch model, not a per-task choice.

right_well.rationale: INPUT_PULLUP: LOW means the beam is broken, i.e. poked. The interpreter inherits verifySensor()'s polarity rather than restating it.

trial_light.rationale: Driven by entry actions on the engagement WAIT_ENTRY (on) and on the zero-duration LIGHTS_OFF nodes (off). Named in no spec for the same reason as odor_port. Its OFF edge is the one that pairs with a behavioural strobe and flips order between paths -- see docs/decisions.md D2.

vacuum.rationale: Closed on entry to a sampling HOLD, which is what routes odor to the port; reopened on the sampling-release WAIT_EXIT. Purely mechanical -- it carries no strobe of its own.

odor_line_7.rationale: Odor solenoid 7. Note the pin ordering is NOT monotonic past line 6 -- 22,24,26,28,30,32 then 23,25,27,29,31,33 -- which is why channels resolve by name and never by arithmetic.

fluid_0.rationale: Left well, reward line 1. `well` is declared so the linter can catch a spec that rewards the left well through a right-well line -- a mistake that would look correct in the listing and deliver water to the wrong side of the box.

fluid_1.rationale: Left well, reward line 2. Unused by every current spec; present because the hardware has it.

fluid_3.rationale: Right well, reward line 2. Unused by every current spec.
